assumptions: Desk is locally flat and level enough for a 42 mm-radius cylinder to rock without catching.
Fingertip press on a 12 mm horn is the intended input; no weighted insert is required for return.
The annular-sector COM formula plus horn bulbs still leaves COM below the outer-arc center; that is an algebraic design check, not a physical cycle receipt.
18 mm thickness is enough that the part does not fall sideways in ordinary desk use; sideways stability is not physically tested here.

components.form: Constant-width crescent: annular sector of outer radius 42 mm and inner radius 30 mm, half-angle 50 deg, capped with tangent 6 mm horn disks, extruded 18 mm, with 0.6 mm dishes on the +Z cheek at each horn.
components.interfaces: None. No mates, fasteners, or purchased parts. Desk contact is the outer cylinder; finger contact is either horn bulb.
components.placement: Arc center at (0, 42) in XY; belly at y=0; horns symmetric about Y. Print origin keeps the bed cheek at Z=0.

concept.construction: Single fused solid from a 2D crescent profile extruded on the cheek. No assembly.
distinctive_features: Circular-arc outer belly so rocking is a single-radius gravity cycle.
Concentric inner cut that makes a readable crescent rather than a filled banana.
Two 6 mm-radius horn bulbs, tangent to inner and outer arcs, as the only press targets.
Shallow 10 mm dishes on the show cheek at each horn so the invitation is visible from across a desk.

envelope_mm.notes: Print coordinates. Length from horn to horn; height from belly to horn crown; thickness is the desk-stable width in use.

concept.intended_interaction: Place the rocker on a desk on its outer belly. Press either rounded horn with a fingertip. The body rolls along the circular belly, the opposite horn rises, then restoring torque from the low center of mass returns it to the centered rest pose. Repeat from the other horn. One-handed; no reset step.
concept.materials: Consumer FDM thermoplastic, one color. Geometry, not paint, carries the crescent and the horn targets.
concept.print_stance: One flat cheek on the bed, crescent silhouette in XY, thickness along +Z, min(Z)=0. Support-free. In use the part is stood on the outer cylindrical belly so the horns point up.
concept.safety: Round horns, no points, no pinch, no stored energy, no small separable parts.
concept.summary: A tiny one-piece crescent desk rocker. Press a rounded horn with a fingertip and it tips, then gravity walks it back to rest on its outer curve.
concept.title: Horn Tip
concept.tolerances: No fits. Solid body. Nominal dimensions are the CAD parameters; print shrinkage is not claimed as measured.
unresolved_risks: Printer elephant-foot on the bed cheek can flatten a sliver of the rocking cylinder; a light brim cleanup may be needed. Not proven until a host print.
Desk friction and exact mass distribution set the number of rocks after a press. Digital geometry cannot claim a specific cycle count or a satisfying feel.
If a future print uses a very high-friction surface, the rocker may stick instead of rolling.
concept.wall_thickness_notes: Solid extruded body. Minimum section is the 12 mm horn diameter and the 12 mm radial crescent width, both far above two 0.4 mm nozzle lines. Not hollowed.

annular-sector-com.claim: The radial center of mass of a concentric annular sector of radii R, r and half-angle alpha is (2/3)(R^3-r^3)/(R^2-r^2) * (sin alpha / alpha) from the arc center. For R=42, r=30, alpha=50 deg this is about 31.9 mm, so COM sits about 10 mm above the desk and 10 mm below the 42 mm curvature center. Horn bulbs at mid-radius sit even closer to the belly, which does not reverse the inequality.
annular-sector-com.source: Standard polar first-moment formula for an annular sector; evaluated on the chosen parameters in assembled.step.py and measure/check_spec.py.

crescent-rocker-cg.claim: Crescent-shaped rockers that keep the center of gravity in the high central body, not out at the horns, are a known way to prevent end-tipping. This product uses that form idea; it is not a copy of the patented exercise rocker.
crescent-rocker-cg.source: US patent 3,227,445 (D. D. Giovanna, 1966), crescent rocker body with center of gravity concentrated centrally to prevent tipping at the ends.

fingertip-pad-scale.claim: An adult finger pad is typically about 10 to 14 mm, and 10 mm x 10 mm is a common minimum touch-target size. Horn diameter 12 mm and 10 mm cheek dishes sit on that scale.
fingertip-pad-scale.source: Dan Saffer, interaction-design talk citing 10-14 mm adult finger pads; Rachel Hinman, The Mobile Frontier (Rosenfeld Media, 2012), 10x14 mm pad and 10x10 mm minimum target.

index-fingertip-width.claim: Measured index-fingertip width around 16 mm supports making the press target a 12 mm horn rather than a needle tip.
index-fingertip-width.source: Kochi University of Technology dissertation data: average index fingertip width 16.0 mm (SD 1.9 mm).

no-purchased-parts.claim: No gear, bearing, fastener, or other catalog component is used. The rocking surface is an authored cylinder, not a bought wheel.
no-purchased-parts.source: Wish constraint: one-piece. CAD skill step-parts search is for purchasable standard elements; none apply.

print-min-wall.claim: A 0.4 mm nozzle needs at least two extruded lines (0.8 mm) before a wall is printable. This part's thinnest designed section is 12 mm, so thickness is a solid-body choice for desk stability, not a shell.
print-min-wall.source: Materialized CAD skill references/print-optimisation.md: cadprint.min_wall(nozzle) is two lines.

rocker-stability-curvature.claim: A rocking rigid body on a smooth curve is stable at an equilibrium where the center of mass lies below the local center of curvature, unstable if above, and neutral if coincident.
rocker-stability-curvature.source: Patrick Glaschke, Tautochrone and Brachistochrone Shape Solutions for Rocking Rigid Bodies, arXiv:1604.03021, 2016, §3 Static Equilibrium.
